messages:
sara: FYI starting traffic-mesh run against eu-west1. Goal: validate admission thresholds and queueing behaviour at 70/85/100% GPU saturation. 30m run. I'll post logs/results here.

sara: injector command:
```
mesh-injector --run-id tm-1779006789 --target eu-west1 --profiles steady,burst --rps 1200-2500 --concurrency 200 --mix "short:60,long:30,superlong:10" --duration 30m
```

loadtester-bot: run started id=tm-1779006789 target=eu-west1 rps=1200->2500 profiles=[steady,burst] duration=30m

jonathan: what's the ramp schedule? are we simulating long sequences or mostly short chats?

sara: mix defined above. long=1024 tokens, superlong=4096. important to exercise KV cache cold misses.

lee: watch metrics: `admitted_rate`, `queue_depth`, `gpu_util`, `p99_latency`. set alert if `queue_depth`>300 for >2m :warning:

priya: can we pin a canary model so fallback doesn't mask admission behavior?

sara: pinned `rwd-7b-v1-8q` for the run (no autoscaling variants). also disabled region-fallback routing to isolate eu-west behavior.

mike: cost FYI — this will burn ~12 GPU-hours in eu-west; budgeted but flagging for finance.

infra-bot: probe: observed node-level network spikes at 17:03 UTC on gw-3 during ramp

loadtester-bot: run finished id=tm-1779006789. summary:
- peak_gpu_sat=96%
- admitted_rate dropped ~38% at peak
- queue_depth max=1124
- drop_rate (admission rejects) rose from 0.2% -> 9.8%
- p99_latency increased 120ms -> 840ms

sara: quick takeaways: admission threshold too permissive under mixed long-tail traffic. queueing grew nonlinearly once `gpu_util` > 90% and GPU-side KV misses amplified token generation time. Proposed immediate changes:
- reduce per-GPU concurrency 96 -> 64
- tighten token-bucket burst size 200 -> 100
- enable aggressive prefix caching / prefetch for long sequences (prefetch_pct=20)

jonathan: +1 on concurrency. also suggest adding adaptive admission that drops superlong requests earlier (cheap heuristic) :thinking:

priya: also want to test region reroute: if eu-west hits red, traffic should smoothly spill to us-central. schedule a failover smoke next week?

sara: yep will schedule. I will run a follow-up with the new thresholds and failover enabled. posting full logs and dashboards in a follow-up message.

mike: thanks — saved the summary and cost note. :thumbsup:
